analysis:
The PR adds a load-time shape warmup (EngineV2Bridge+ShapeWarmup.swift), a faster calibration-prompt search (CalibrationPrompt.swift:19-34), a per-cell timeout and sampled-temperature option (ModelCalibrationRequests.swift:4-10, 51-52), and a reclaim-sweep skip while a calibration session is active (GlobalKVCacheBudget.swift:380). I found no regression against the A-001, A-003, A-010, A-016 or T-041 areas.

Data exposure: warmup and calibration prompts are built-in text rendered locally. They are submitted with cacheEnabled:false, so nothing is written to the SSD prefix cache (T-041 unchanged). The log line at ShapeWarmup.swift:128 records only model ID, counts and timings. No consumer data or keys are involved.

Authorization and attestation: warmup runs through the existing idle-calibration session (startIfIdle, canSubmitWithNativeOwner, posture checks). It touches no coordinator, App Attest or serving-authorization state (TB-011, A-016). The startup preload (runShapeWarmupBeforeServing) runs before registration. It is bounded by shapeWarmupBudgetSeconds (20s per the docs) and by cancellation, so it adds only bounded startup latency (availability, minor).

Calibration prompt search: the division at line 32 is guarded by tokens.count > one. Planned probes are clamped to [low, high], and each probe narrows the bounds, so the loop terminates with the same result semantics as before. The timeout is clamped by max(0, …) and the interrupt guard is unchanged.

Availability: skipping reclaimer.scheduleSweep while idleCalibration.hasSession is true defers memory reclaim. This is safe only if hasSession is always cleared on retirement or cancellation. That is unverified because the idleCalibration source was not supplied; a stuck session could suppress reclaim, which is memory-pressure and DoS-relevant but not demonstrated.

Unverified external contracts: ModelCalibrationPolicy (shapeWarmup, shaderCacheProbe, the cell.sampled and warmup flags, shaderCacheLooksCold) and the claim that warmup cells move no rate or counter. docs/reference/configuration.md only documents the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP variable (a head-text excerpt of that file was supplied); it is not a security control.
